_doc: Symptom card warning signs (docs/design/symptom-context-card.md section 7). Generic defaults transcribed from public NHS pages (checked 07-Nov-2026); tiers per the family context rules (A: 999/A&E items; B: urgent GP/111 and GP items). NOT clinical guidance for a person: status stays pending_clinician_signoff until the treating doctor reviews the records-side copy. Modifiers are read from the KB; a rule applies when all its 'when' modifiers hold.

nhs-rashes.title: Rashes in babies and children (hives section applies to adults)

modifiers.name: a stroke on record in the last 180 days

rules.owner: Headache that started suddenly and is extremely painful.
rules.family: A sudden, very bad headache.

rules.owner: Headache with numbness or weakness of the face or body, difficulty speaking, balancing or walking, drowsiness or confusion, or a fit.
rules.family: Headache with a weak or numb face, arm or leg, trouble speaking or walking, or being very sleepy or confused.

rules.owner: Headache with loss of vision, or with a very high temperature and a stiff neck, or bright light hurting the eyes.
rules.family: Headache with loss of sight, or with high fever and a stiff neck.

rules.owner: Headache with vision or eye problems, with vomiting, or made worse by coughing, sneezing or bending down.
rules.family: Headache with eye trouble or vomiting, or worse on coughing or bending.

rules.owner: Any change in sight (wavy lines, flashing, loss of vision), light hurting the eyes, or one pupil bigger than the other.
rules.family: Any change in sight, or light hurting the eyes.

rules.owner: Eye very dark red, a severe headache with feeling sick, or an injury or chemical in the eye.
rules.family: A very dark red eye, a bad headache with feeling sick, or something got into the eye.

rules.owner: Eye very painful and red.
rules.family: A painful red eye.

rules.owner: Red eyes with a sticky discharge, or red patches in the eye lasting more than a few days.
rules.family: Sticky discharge, or redness lasting more than a few days.

rules.owner: On a blood thinner: a red patch on the white of the eye. Show a doctor within the week; with pain, a change in sight or other bleeding it is Tier A.
rules.family: On the blood thinner: a red patch on the eye. Show a doctor this week.

rules.owner: Sudden chest pain or discomfort that does not go away (squeezing, pressure, burning, or like indigestion).
rules.family: Chest pain or pressure that does not go away.

rules.owner: Chest pain spreading to an arm, the neck, jaw, stomach or back, or with sweating, feeling sick, light-headed or short of breath.
rules.family: Chest pain going into the arm, neck or jaw, or with sweating or breathlessness.

rules.owner: Chest pain that comes and goes.
rules.family: Chest pain that comes and goes.

rules.owner: Heart palpitations: racing, too slow, skipping or fluttering.
rules.family: The heart racing or fluttering.

rules.owner: Stomach pain that started suddenly and is severe.
rules.family: A sudden, severe stomach pain.

rules.owner: Vomiting blood or vomit like coffee grounds; a lot of blood from the bottom, or black, sticky stool.
rules.family: Blood in vomit, or black or bloody stool.

rules.owner: Cannot pass urine at all, or cannot pass stool or wind at all.
rules.family: Not able to pass urine, or stool and wind, at all.

rules.owner: Diarrhoea or vomiting not gone after a few days, blood in the stool, or pain that suddenly gets much worse.
rules.family: Loose motions or vomiting that do not settle in a few days.

rules.owner: Lips, mouth, throat or tongue suddenly swollen, a tight throat, trouble swallowing or breathing very fast.
rules.family: Lips, tongue or throat swelling, or trouble breathing or swallowing.

rules.owner: A rash like small bruises or bleeding under the skin that does not fade when a glass is pressed on it.
rules.family: A rash like small bruises that does not fade under a pressed glass.

rules.owner: Face drooping on one side, weakness or numbness in one arm or leg, slurred or confused speech, even if it passes (FAST).
rules.family: Face drooping, a weak arm or leg, or speech changing, even if it passes.

rules.owner: Sudden blurred vision or loss of sight, sudden confusion, or dizziness with falling over.
rules.family: Sudden loss of sight, sudden confusion, or falling over with dizziness.

rules.owner: After the recent stroke: any new or returning weakness, numbness, speech change, double vision or loss of sight, even if brief.
rules.family: Any new weakness, speech change or seeing double, even if it passes.

rules.owner: Severe difficulty breathing (gasping, choking, cannot get words out), chest tight or heavy, lips or skin pale, blue or grey, or sudden confusion.
rules.family: Struggling to breathe or speak, or lips turning blue or grey.

rules.owner: More short of breath than usual, coughing up blood, or pain or swelling in one leg.
rules.family: More breathless than usual, or one leg painful or swollen.

rules.owner: With the weak heart on record: passing out and not responding normally, or severe difficulty breathing.
rules.family: Fainting, or struggling to breathe.

rules.owner: With the weak heart on record: breathless lying down or with everyday activity, coughing up frothy pink phlegm, or sudden weight gain.
rules.family: Breathless when lying flat, or weight going up quickly.

rules.owner: Urine symptoms with confusion, drowsiness or difficulty speaking.
rules.family: Confused or very sleepy.

rules.owner: Urine symptoms at 65 or older, with a high or low temperature or shivering, pain low in the tummy or in the back under the ribs, blood in the urine, or not better within 2 days.
rules.family: Fever or shivering, back pain, blood in the urine, or not better in 2 days.

rules.owner: Dizziness that does not go away or keeps coming back, or with changes to the pulse, fainting, headaches, double or blurred vision, or numbness.
rules.family: Dizziness that keeps coming back, or with fainting.

rules.owner: On a blood thinner: blood in the urine, stool or vomit, coughing up blood, or a sudden bad headache with confusion, light hurting the eyes or slurred speech.
rules.family: On the blood thinner: blood in urine, stool or vomit, or a sudden bad headache with confusion.
